The '''Players Committee''' (PC) is the volunteer group that took over support of ''Star Wars'' CCG from Decipher in 2002. It created Virtual cards, reorganized them into Virtual Blocks in 2009, and Reset the tournament pool in 2014. For rules by era see [[Rulebooks]]; for constructed pools see [[Formats]]; for Virtual packaging eras see [[Decipher era]], [[Virtual Original]], [[Virtual Legacy]] and [[Virtual Modern]].

== Timeline (high level) ==

=== Decipher era and handoff ===

Decipher published ''Star Wars'' CCG from 1995 through [[Theed Palace]] (2001) and related products. When Decipher announced the license was leaving, it publicly formed a '''Players' Committee''' / Player Advocate structure so fans could continue organized play, rulings, and support.<ref name="pc1">[https://web.archive.org/web/20020611042314/http://decipher.com/starwars/playerscommittee1.html The Star Wars Players' Committee], decipher.com (Wayback, 11 June 2002; letter dated 25 January 2002)</ref> In a Lucasfilm form letter posted by [[Game Players Network]] on 8 January 2002, [[Howard Roffman]] wrote that Decipher would not produce new ''Star Wars'' products and that Decipher had committed to continue the existing games for as long as the player community wanted to play them.<ref name="gpn-roffman">[http://www.gameplayersnetwork.com/card/news.asp?gm=starwars&id=58 Lucasfilm Comments on Star Wars License], Game Players Network (posted 8 January 2002). Preserved copy: [https://web.archive.org/web/20040903190722/http://www.gameplayersnetwork.com/card/news.asp?gm=starwars&id=58 Internet Archive]</ref>

[[Warren Holland]] first outlined the committee in a ''[[Radio Free Decipher]]'' special broadcast on 28 December 2001, the day the end of the license was announced. He described a non-profit, all-volunteer "Players Committee for Star Wars CCGs" of top players and playtesters, which Decipher would support free of charge with email, listserv, web and office facilities. It would be the community's voice on the game's future and oversee rules support and FAQs. At the end of April 2002 Decipher would turn over tournament prize support, the web pages and World Championship duties, and donate reference cards. The committee would also choose existing cards and post replacement game text for them to make them tournament legal, and would become self-governing once its members were selected.<ref>[https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=ZpXfkPyurfE&t=1332s Radio Free Decipher Special Broadcast (28 December, 2001): Warren Holland and the Players Committee], Player's Council, YouTube (uploaded 18 February 2022), at 22:12. Preserved copy: [https://archive.org/details/youtube-ZpXfkPyurfE Internet Archive]. Transcript: [[Radio Free Decipher/Special Broadcast (28 December 2001) transcript]].</ref> By 11 January 2002 just over 200 people had applied; Decipher said the names of applicants not chosen would be passed to the committee.<ref>[https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=8aNpe-I-KQk&t=90s Broadcast 110 - Radio Free Decipher (11 January, 2002): SWCCG Player's Committee, ST/LOTR News], Player's Council, YouTube (uploaded 13 May 2022), at 01:30. Preserved copy: [https://archive.org/details/youtube-8aNpe-I-KQk Internet Archive]. Transcript: [[Radio Free Decipher/Episode 110 transcript]].</ref>

Decipher's Star Wars Announcement page invited players to '''volunteer for the players' committee'''. It listed a volunteer contact alongside [[Warren Holland|Holland]]/Jones and Lucas Licensing contacts, and linked the 25 January 2002 Players' Committee announcement.<ref name="deciphercall">[https://web.archive.org/web/20020601152726/http://decipher.com/starwars/announcement122801.html The Star Wars Announcement], decipher.com (Wayback, 1 June 2002)</ref> The PC Advocates came from that call for volunteers.

On '''25 January 2002''', [[Warren Holland]] (Chairman &amp; CEO) announced the '''first team of Star Wars Player Advocates''' on Decipher's Players' Committee page.<ref name="pc1" /> The letter names Advocate roles for player, tournament, rules and gameplay support. It describes a Norfolk meeting to turn the game over to players and teases a forthcoming virtual-card pool and timetable. Game Players Network would help with communications and prize shipping after 30 April 2002.<ref name="pc1" />

Advocate and Advocate Council rosters are listed on [[Players Committee advocates]]. They run from the first six Advocates and early Council members such as [[Doug Taylor]], [[Josh Radke]] and [[John Arendt]] to the PC organization charts of 2021 and 2024.

On '''29 April 2002''', Game Players Network reported that Decipher would donate over one million dollars in product, promotional materials and financial backing to the Players Committee.<ref name="gpn2002">[https://web.archive.org/web/20020610202816/http://www.gameplayersnetwork.com/card/games.asp?gm=starwars Game Players Network - Star Wars CCG index], Wayback 10 June 2002</ref>

=== Virtual program begins (2002) ===

The PC announced its '''first Virtual Card Set''' on '''12 February 2002''', targeting release on '''4 March 2002''' and Virtual Set #2 on '''6 May 2002'''. Previews ran 25 February-1 March 2002, and the cards were distributed as PDFs on decipher.com.<ref name="tfn2002">[https://theforce.net/ccg/story/Players_Committee_Announces_the_First_Virtual_Card_Set_68946.asp Player's Committee Announces the First Virtual Card Set], TheForce.Net, 12 February 2002. Preserved copy: [https://web.archive.org/web/20261020214905/https://theforce.net/ccg/story/Players_Committee_Announces_the_First_Virtual_Card_Set_68946.asp Internet Archive].</ref>

Virtual Card Set #1, released on '''5 March 2002''', had twelve Premiere-based (V) slips and became '''tournament-legal on Saturday, 9 March 2002'''.<ref name="decivs1">[https://web.archive.org/web/20020610072829/http://www.decipher.com/starwars/playerscommittee/virtualcardset1.html Virtual Card Set #1 is Away!], decipher.com (Wayback)</ref>

The early printable slips used a modifier/sleeve presentation very different from later Block-era and current Virtual packaging.<ref name="vc1pdf">[https://web.archive.org/web/20050813215254/http://decipher.com/starwars/cardlists/virtual/VirtualCards1.pdf VirtualCards1.pdf], decipher.com (Wayback, 13 August 2005)</ref>

From 2002 to 2009 the PC released '''numbered Virtual Sets''' and [[Virtual Set: Defensive Shields|Defensive Shields]].<ref name="swpl">[https://star-wars.pl/Tekst/1963,Star_Wars_CCG_Virtual_Sets.html Star Wars CCG Virtual Sets], star-wars.pl (chronology). Preserved copy: [https://web.archive.org/web/20261008192957/https://star-wars.pl/Tekst/1963,Star_Wars_CCG_Virtual_Sets.html Internet Archive].</ref> The era hub is [[Virtual Original]]. The set index is on [[Virtual Sets (2002-2009)]]. The consolidated rules book from 2007 is [[Players Committee Advanced Rulebook 1.7.1]].

=== Young Jedi, Jedi Knights and promotions (2002) ===

In 2002 [[Young Jedi]] also received the virtual treatment: the PC wrote new text for many text-less cards and tweaked the rules to make play more fluid. [[Jedi Knights Trading Card Game|Jedi Knights]] received no virtual cards. Instead its sanctioned league was relaunched, with kits for tournament directors, and an extensive FAQ dealt with issues left open after the last expansion. Collector packs sold in chain stores, with cards from all three of Decipher's ''Star Wars'' games, gave many players their first look at Jedi Knights. Promotions that year included Femme Fatale in June and, in the summer, the Flashback promotion, which went back to the [[Premiere]] expansion.<ref name="pc-bruun02">[http://www.swccgpc.com/News/duane2002yearend.htm The State Of SWCCG], Duane Bruun (PC Staff Writer), swccgpc.com (2002). Preserved copy: [https://web.archive.org/web/20030613110815/http://swccgpc.com:80/News/duane2002yearend.htm Internet Archive]</ref>

Looking back on 2002, the PC described itself as "the first player run organization to have full control over the future of a CCG".<ref name="pc-roadtoworlds03">[http://www.swccgpc.com/News/Events/2003/roadtoworlds03.htm Road to Worlds Begins in 2003; SWCCG Player's Committee Announces Strategic Partnership], swccgpc.com (2002). Preserved copy: [https://web.archive.org/web/20040620161313/http://www.swccgpc.com:80/News/Events/2003/roadtoworlds03.htm Internet Archive]</ref>

=== Forum years (2003–2005) ===

On 27 January 2003 [[Jason Robinette]], posting as JasonRed3, asked players not to post dream cards, real or virtual, on the Players Committee forum; lists of cards players wanted virtualized were still allowed.<ref name="pcf-750-12379">[http://www.swccgpc.com/forums/viewtopic.php?p=12379#12379 Polite Reminder], JasonRed3, Players Committee forum, swccgpc.com (27 January 2003). Preserved copy: [https://web.archive.org/web/20040714231157/http://www.swccgpc.com:80/forums/viewtopic.php?p=12379%26amp Internet Archive]</ref> Replying to complaints, [[Greg Zinn]] pointed out that the volunteers worked for free and that neither Decipher, which could no longer sell cards, nor the Committee made any money from virtual cards.<ref name="pcf-750-12401">[http://www.swccgpc.com/forums/viewtopic.php?p=12401#12401 Polite Reminder], Gergall, Players Committee forum, swccgpc.com (27 January 2003). Preserved copy: [https://web.archive.org/web/20040714231157/http://www.swccgpc.com:80/forums/viewtopic.php?p=12379%26amp Internet Archive]</ref> On 29 January 2003 [[Doug Taylor]], Player Advocate for card design, wrote that fewer than 1% of the virtual cards so far owed their text to dream-card threads, and that Decipher had spent many hours one weekend "passing the torch" to the Committee. New cards were tested by top players and then checked by the QA team and Rules Committee; [[Blizzard 2 (V)]] went through 11 versions.<ref name="pcf-750-12886">[http://www.swccgpc.com/forums/viewtopic.php?p=12886#12886 Polite Reminder], DougRed4, Players Committee forum, swccgpc.com (29 January 2003). Preserved copy: [https://web.archive.org/web/20050228113751/http://www.swccgpc.com:80/forums/viewtopic.php?p=12576%26amp Internet Archive]</ref>

In September 2003, after [[Andrew Howard]] stepped down as Tournament Advocate, players nominated successors on the forum, among them [[Scott Lingrell]], [[Nick Kolnik]], [[Josh Radke]] and [[Jim Colson]].<ref name="pcf-2188-33226">[http://www.swccgpc.com/forums/viewtopic.php?p=33226#33226 New Tournament Advocate], Pistone84, Players Committee forum, swccgpc.com (17 September 2003). Preserved copy: [https://web.archive.org/web/20040112231657/http://www.swccgpc.com:80/forums/viewtopic.php?p=36534%26amp Internet Archive]</ref><ref name="pcf-2188-33233">[http://www.swccgpc.com/forums/viewtopic.php?p=33233#33233 New Tournament Advocate], Gergall, Players Committee forum, swccgpc.com (17 September 2003). Preserved copy: [https://web.archive.org/web/20040112231657/http://www.swccgpc.com:80/forums/viewtopic.php?p=36534%26amp Internet Archive]</ref><ref name="pcf-2188-33236">[http://www.swccgpc.com/forums/viewtopic.php?p=33236#33236 New Tournament Advocate], Pistone84, Players Committee forum, swccgpc.com (17 September 2003). Preserved copy: [https://web.archive.org/web/20040112231657/http://www.swccgpc.com:80/forums/viewtopic.php?p=36534%26amp Internet Archive]</ref><ref name="pcf-2188-33321">[http://www.swccgpc.com/forums/viewtopic.php?p=33321#33321 New Tournament Advocate], Shadow 29, Players Committee forum, swccgpc.com (18 September 2003). Preserved copy: [https://web.archive.org/web/20040112231657/http://www.swccgpc.com:80/forums/viewtopic.php?p=36534%26amp Internet Archive]</ref> Howard wrote that he had attended all the major conventions and run the big events, including the 2002 and 2003 World Championships, at his own expense, as the Committee did not have the funds.<ref name="pcf-2188-33299">[http://www.swccgpc.com/forums/viewtopic.php?p=33299#33299 New Tournament Advocate], Andrew Howard, Players Committee forum, swccgpc.com (18 September 2003). Preserved copy: [https://web.archive.org/web/20040112231657/http://www.swccgpc.com:80/forums/viewtopic.php?p=36534%26amp Internet Archive]</ref> By November 2003 [[Mitch Velasco]] led the tournament work, with Radke working with him.<ref name="pcf-2188-36534">[http://www.swccgpc.com/forums/viewtopic.php?p=36534#36534 New Tournament Advocate], The_Big_Shot_009, Players Committee forum, swccgpc.com (16 November 2003). Preserved copy: [https://web.archive.org/web/20040112231657/http://www.swccgpc.com:80/forums/viewtopic.php?p=36534%26amp Internet Archive]</ref>

In November 2003 Radke, of the Tournaments Department, proposed Players Committee Invitationals for 2004: Battle of Naboo (UK), Coruscant Invitational (New York City), Bespin Invitational (Minnesota or Chicago) and Battle of Endor (Seattle), with an Alderaan Invitational (Gen Con SoCal) and a Mon Calamari Invitational (Australia) considered for 2005. Players would qualify with a rating of 1650 or more or a first or second place at another PC Championship event that year; entry would cost $10–20, and prizes would include cash, collectibles and byes to Day 2.<ref name="pcf-2355-35763">[http://www.swccgpc.com/forums/viewtopic.php?p=35763#35763 Invitationals Poll], Red84, Players Committee forum, swccgpc.com (9 November 2003). Preserved copy: [https://web.archive.org/web/20040323102043/http://www.swccgpc.com:80/forums/viewtopic.php?t=2355%26amp Internet Archive]</ref> Because many tournament directors had raised the concern that a ratings cut-off would leave out communities that did not use Decipher's tournament system, he said the Invitationals would stay open until the Committee had its own independent ratings system.<ref name="pcf-2355-35811">[http://www.swccgpc.com/forums/viewtopic.php?p=35811#35811 Invitationals Poll], Red84, Players Committee forum, swccgpc.com (9 November 2003). Preserved copy: [https://web.archive.org/web/20040323102043/http://www.swccgpc.com:80/forums/viewtopic.php?t=2355%26amp Internet Archive]</ref> He noted that DPCs were held every year in Atlanta, Las Vegas and Orlando.<ref name="pcf-2355-35785">[http://www.swccgpc.com/forums/viewtopic.php?p=35785#35785 Invitationals Poll], Red84, Players Committee forum, swccgpc.com (9 November 2003). Preserved copy: [https://web.archive.org/web/20040323102043/http://www.swccgpc.com:80/forums/viewtopic.php?t=2355%26amp Internet Archive]</ref>

On 24 May 2004 the main site announced [[Kevin Brownell]] and Nick Kolnik as the two new advocates, together with a new "webgroup".<ref name="pcf-3349-46706">[http://www.swccgpc.com/forums/viewtopic.php?p=46706#46706 Congrats to the new Advocates!], Jedi K, Players Committee forum, swccgpc.com (24 May 2004). Preserved copy: [https://web.archive.org/web/20040625212439/http://www.swccgpc.com:80/forums/viewtopic.php?p=46930%26amp Internet Archive]</ref><ref name="pcf-3349-46715">[http://www.swccgpc.com/forums/viewtopic.php?p=46715#46715 Congrats to the new Advocates!], Rustan Sharer, Players Committee forum, swccgpc.com (24 May 2004). Preserved copy: [https://web.archive.org/web/20040625212439/http://www.swccgpc.com:80/forums/viewtopic.php?p=46930%26amp Internet Archive]</ref> In November 2004 players again asked for a ratings system independent of Decipher's.<ref name="pcf-4111-56328">[http://www.swccgpc.com/forums/viewtopic.php?p=56328#56328 Ratings?], Tim Simon, Players Committee forum, swccgpc.com (15 November 2004). Preserved copy: [https://web.archive.org/web/20041227070836/http://www.swccgpc.com:80/forums/viewtopic.php?p=56333%26amp Internet Archive]</ref> In January 2005 Brownell explained that the virtual-set PDFs had been password-protected because someone had made convincing "dream" virtual cards by editing an unprotected PDF.<ref name="pcf-4354-59480">[http://www.swccgpc.com/forums/viewtopic.php?p=59480#59480 Virtual Cards], Kevin Brownell, Players Committee forum, swccgpc.com (5 January 2005). Preserved copy: [https://web.archive.org/web/20050228234025/http://www.swccgpc.com:80/forums/viewtopic.php?p=59576%26amp Internet Archive]</ref> That month tournament directors who wanted sanctioned events registered as tournament directors on Decipher's site for a $1 fee,<ref name="pcf-4463-60644">[http://www.swccgpc.com/forums/viewtopic.php?p=60644#60644 need help doing tournaments], Steve Sanders, Players Committee forum, swccgpc.com (24 January 2005). Preserved copy: [https://web.archive.org/web/20050226015125/http://www.swccgpc.com:80/forums/viewtopic.php?p=60683%26amp Internet Archive]</ref> and Kolnik asked players to link their tournament reports on DeckTech and [[Game Players Network|GPN]], for example in their forum signatures, rather than post them on the forum.<ref name="pcf-4472-60722">[http://www.swccgpc.com/forums/viewtopic.php?p=60722#60722 Tournament Reports], Nick Kolnik, Players Committee forum, swccgpc.com (25 January 2005). Preserved copy: [https://web.archive.org/web/20050217013758/http://www.swccgpc.com:80/forums/viewtopic.php?p=60771%26amp Internet Archive]</ref>

=== Reorg / "Blocks" (about September 2009) ===

Main articles: [[2009 Virtual Block Reorganization]], [[Virtual Legacy]].

In 2009 the PC reorganized the '''previous 18 virtual sets''' into six thematic blocks, with '''Official text as of 7 December 2009'''.<ref name="blockreorg">[https://res.starwarsccg.org/legacyblocks/VirtualBlock1.pdf VirtualBlock1.pdf]. Preserved copy: [https://web.archive.org/web/20261020181626/https://res.starwarsccg.org/legacyblocks/VirtualBlock1.pdf Internet Archive].</ref> Block releases continued after the reorganization, such as Block 6.3 Mercenaries on '''15 March 2010'''.<ref name="swpl" />

The official slips library lists '''Legacy Virtual Sets (2002-2009)''' separately from '''Legacy Virtual Blocks (2009-2014)'''.<ref name="slips">[https://www.starwarsccg.org/resources/virtual-slips/ Virtual Slips / Files], starwarsccg.org. Preserved copy: [https://web.archive.org/web/20240920164229/https://www.starwarsccg.org/resources/virtual-slips/ Internet Archive].</ref>

Block pages are [[Virtual Block 1]]-[[Virtual Block 9]] and [[Virtual Shields]]; the era overview is [[Virtual Legacy]]. The set index is [[Virtual Blocks (2009-2014)]]. Blocks were not a lossless rename of VS1-18: presentation, organization, errata and the legal card pool could change. Virtual cards could be '''dropped''' far more easily than physical product could be reprinted.

=== Advanced Rulebook 1.7.1 (Original Virtual rules) ===

[[Players Committee Advanced Rulebook 1.7.1]] (PDF dated 6 July 2007) replaced previous rulebooks. The Players Committee rules page linked that PDF in July and September 2009.<ref name="pcrules2009">[https://web.archive.org/web/20090706102757/http://www.starwarsccg.org/rules/ Rules], starwarsccg.org (Wayback, 6 July 2009)</ref> The January 2003 [[Players Committee Rules Supplement (2003)|Rules Supplement]] is the earlier PC layer on the Decipher core books.

=== Advanced Rulebook 2.0 (Legacy Virtual rules) ===

During the Legacy Virtual period the PC published [[Players Committee Advanced Rulebook 2.0]]. Among other revisions it introduced the [[Mission]] card type. That book is '''not''' the current tournament Advanced Rulebook.

=== 2014 Virtual Card Reset ===

In '''Fall 2014''' the PC Reset the competitive virtual pool; [[Virtual Set 0]] and [[Virtual Set D]] are dated '''24 September 2014'''. The Alternate Format Tournament Guide separates '''Standard''' (post-Reset virtual icons) from '''Legacy''' (the pre-Reset black-diamond / Block pool). It names the 2014 World Championships as the last championship circuit on the old pool.<ref name="afg">[https://res.starwarsccg.org/wp/wp-content/uploads/Alternate-Formats-Guide.pdf Alternate Format Tournament Guide] (revised 09/2015), via [[Formats]]. Preserved copy: [https://web.archive.org/web/20261008195355/https://res.starwarsccg.org/wp/wp-content/uploads/Alternate-Formats-Guide.pdf Internet Archive].</ref>

Current Virtual sets have continued since the Reset ([[:Category:Current Virtual sets]]). The current tournament rules are the [[Players Committee Advanced Rulebook]] (2023 edition).

=== Current site ===

An early official Players Committee website was '''swccgpc.com''', which carried news by October 2002.<ref name="swccgpc2002">[https://web.archive.org/web/20021106101746/http://www.swccgpc.com/ The SWCCG Player's Committee], swccgpc.com (Wayback, 6 November 2002)</ref>

On '''10 June 2009''', the PC moved to a new server and began forwarding to its new domain, '''StarWarsCCG.org'''.<ref name="domain2009">[https://web.archive.org/web/20090706102740/http://www.starwarsccg.org/news/news.php?id=69 New Domain and Server], starwarsccg.org news.php?id=69 (posted 10 June 2009; Wayback capture 6 July 2009)</ref>

Organized play, slips, formats and news remain at [https://www.starwarsccg.org/ starwarsccg.org].<ref name="pcsite">[https://www.starwarsccg.org/ Star Wars CCG Players Committee], starwarsccg.org home page. Preserved copy: [https://web.archive.org/web/20250316151226/https://www.starwarsccg.org/ Internet Archive] (capture of 16 March 2025).</ref>

'''Errata and drops:''' Virtual text is easier to revise or remove from legality than a physical print run. A card's (V) text in 2002, its Block-era presentation and any current Virtual descendant may differ, so the current cardlist does not always show the historical text.
